$comment: GATING FOR PROMOTION, NON-BLOCKING FOR GENERATION. Rules how a Suppress selection containing ABLATE reaches publication. Changes no frozen grid, protocol, identity, threshold or prompt artifact.

supersedes.reason: v1.0.0's central claim was FALSE. It asserted that operation lives on a per-strength Spec, that a mixed CLAMP+ABLATE triple therefore already encodes, and that no schema change is required. The accepted input schema does not have that shape. v1.0.0 was written from the reconciliation ruling's prose without opening the accepted schema fixture; the dispatch's description was correct and was contradicted on a false basis.
supersedes.withdrawn_instruction: v1.0.0 directed Engineer 3 to move operation from DirectionRecord back onto Spec. THAT INSTRUCTION IS WITHDRAWN. It would have been a substantial rewrite of a schema that has passed gating three times, justified by a premise that was wrong.

accepted_schema_as_it_actually_is.consistency: All three accepted revisions carry the identical calibration shape. This is a settled design, not drift.

calibration_direction_shape.strengths: {low, medium, high}, each a BARE NUMBER > 0 -- not an object, not a per-strength Spec
calibration_direction_shape.targets: array of {feature_idx, weight}; ablate_weight must be exactly 1.0

accepted_schema_as_it_actually_is.consequence: A mixed CLAMP+ABLATE triple is GENUINELY UNENCODABLE. An ablate direction has no strengths at all -- the schema prohibits the key. There is no place for a per-strength operation to live.
accepted_schema_as_it_actually_is.the_design_is_coherent: The schema expresses a real semantic distinction rather than an oversight: suppression is EITHER a graded clamp with three magnitudes OR a single full ablation. ABLATE is a switch, not the top of a dial, and the schema declines to present it as one.

RULING_publication_candidate_set.rule: S5 / ABLATE IS NOT ELIGIBLE FOR THE PUBLISHED LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH TRIPLE. The published Suppress direction is operation=clamp with three CLAMP strengths drawn from S1..S4.

PRE_REGISTERED_BEFORE_SELECTION.requirement: The restriction binds at SELECTION time, not at publication time. The candidate set for the PUBLISHED triple is S1..S4 from the outset.
PRE_REGISTERED_BEFORE_SELECTION.why_this_matters_more_than_anything_else: Restricting the candidate set BEFORE selection is not substitution. Selecting S5 and then publishing something else WOULD BE. The whole difference between a legitimate constraint and post-hoc dose substitution is whether the constraint existed before the judged scores did. It does now, and no scores exist yet.

S5_remains_fully_scientific: generated in the allocation, all five doses, unchanged
judged with the sweep and with confirmation if selected scientifically
recorded in the selection record and the manifest
reported as the strongest suppression achieved
eligible to satisfy G-E for the purpose of the scientific finding
RULING_publication_candidate_set.what_S5_may_not_do: Occupy low, medium or high in a published calibration direction.

if_no_three_CLAMP_doses_clear_G_E.outcome: Suppress does not publish. suppress = null in both generation_manifests and selection_records, per the standing nullity rule.
if_no_three_CLAMP_doses_clear_G_E.the_finding_is_still_real: 'Only full ablation suppressed this concept' is an honest and interesting result, reported from the validation evidence. A direction that fails to publish is not a direction that failed to produce knowledge.
if_no_three_CLAMP_doses_clear_G_E.already_ruled: This is the existing Amplify-only publication path. Nothing new is required to support it.

supersedes_one_line_of_the_grid_ruling.text_affected: 'ABLATE is ELIGIBLE to be selected as HIGH and will often be'
supersedes_one_line_of_the_grid_ruling.correction: That remains true for the SCIENTIFIC selection recorded in the selection record. It is NOT true for the PUBLISHED triple, whose candidate set is S1..S4.
supersedes_one_line_of_the_grid_ruling.unchanged_and_still_binding: A published Suppress triple whose HIGH is S4 is valid and must not be rejected as malformed. That was the grid ruling's actual point and it survives intact -- indeed it is now the normal case.
supersedes_one_line_of_the_grid_ruling.grid_artifact_not_edited: causal_dose_grid.json is unmodified. This artifact is normative over that one clause.

no_schema_change.verdict: NO CHANGE to the accepted input schema.
reasoning: The schema has passed gating at three successive commits and has fixtures, a validator and gating reports built on it.
The only shape it cannot express is one the publication candidate set now excludes.
Zero concepts have been published, so the restriction costs nothing already banked.
Changing the core calibration shape days from the deadline, for a case now ruled out of scope, is not a trade worth making.
no_schema_change.weights_already_correct: The schema's targets.ablate_weight = 'must be exactly 1.0' already matches the standing weight ruling. v1.0.0's weight analysis was consistent with the schema even though its operation analysis was not.

ablate_only_direction_is_expressible.observation: The schema DOES support a whole direction with operation=ablate, no strengths, weights 1.0.
ablate_only_direction_is_expressible.what_it_would_mean: A Suppress direction that is only full ablation, with no Low/Medium/High dial.
ablate_only_direction_is_expressible.researcher_question: Whether the public tool should ever expose an ablate-only Suppress direction -- a switch rather than a dial -- is a product decision about the demo surface, not a scientific one. I am not deciding it. If it is wanted, it needs its own UI treatment, because the public control is currently Low/Medium/High and an ablate-only direction has no such positions.

never_substitute.rule: The selection record is authoritative and unedited. Publishing a dose other than one the selection procedure selected is prohibited.
never_substitute.how_this_ruling_stays_consistent_with_it: By restricting the candidate set BEFORE selection rather than diverging from the result afterwards. Nothing selected is ever replaced.

generate_all_five.rule: All five Suppress doses S1..S5 are generated in the GPU allocation. Unchanged.
generate_all_five.why: Generation precedes selection. Withholding S5 would remove the evidence for the strongest suppression the arm can produce, which is scientifically the most informative point even though it is not publishable as a triple member.

evidence_producer_text.defect: The evidence producer states 'Suppress HIGH is ABLATE'.
evidence_producer_text.correction: FALSE, and now doubly so. HIGH is a CLAMP dose from S1..S4 selected by the judged sweep. ABLATE is never a published triple member.
evidence_producer_text.also_correct: Any text implying S1..S5 is a continuous magnitude ramp. S1..S4 are CLAMP magnitudes; S5 is a different operation and is not on the same scale.

sequencing.generation: PROCEED NOW, unchanged, all five doses both directions.
sequencing.before_selection_record_implementation: Implement the S1..S4 candidate restriction for the PUBLISHED triple. The selection record still records the full scientific picture including S5.
sequencing.before_promotion: Evidence-producer text corrected. No schema change.

unchanged_artifacts.$comment: Verified byte-identical when this artifact was committed.

hard_stops: S5 or ABLATE occupying low, medium or high in a published calibration direction.
Restricting the published candidate set AFTER any judged score exists -- the restriction is pre-registered or it is substitution.
Publishing a dose other than one the selection procedure selected.
Withholding S5 from generation or from judging.
Rejecting a published Suppress triple whose HIGH is S4.
Any assertion that Suppress HIGH is ABLATE.
Editing the accepted input schema on the strength of superseded ruling v1.0.0.
